metadata.title: Intent and Motivation Framework
metadata.description: A cross-domain reviewer knowledge pack for intent and motivation reasoning, including indirect encouragement, indirect threat, praise, mockery, and normalization when context recovers the meaning.

pack.title: Intent and Motivation Framework
pack.purpose: Teach reviewers how to recognize intent and motivation across domains before legal classification.
required_evidence: Target or audience of the statement
Context that recovers indirect encouragement, indirect threat, or other implied intent
insufficient_evidence: A single isolated sentence without context
Guessing motive from one ambiguous word
Assuming harmful intent without speaker support
reviewer_heuristics: Read the scene before assigning intent.
Separate literal wording from implied motivation.
Treat documentary/documentation and educational framing as informational rather than promotional.
Treat encouragement and threat as possibly indirect when the surrounding context, speaker-target relationship, or later dialogue makes the meaning recoverable.
Check whether later dialogue reverses the first impression.
Treat quotation, acting, storytelling, and documentary framing as possible non-literal or non-evaluative frames.
Treat mockery as expressive or satirical unless the scene clearly uses it as direct endorsement.
Treat praise, glorification, and normalization as evaluative signals that can strengthen promotion or approval when the context supports them.
Use confidence to reflect ambiguity instead of overclaiming.
positive_examples: A line that clearly expresses threat, approval, or encouragement.
A statement that remains informative but becomes meaningful through later context.
A scene where a character confesses intent in plain language.
A line that only becomes an encouragement after the follow-up response.
A line that only becomes a threat once the target and context are visible.
negative_examples: A harmless factual sentence treated as a threat.
A quoted line treated as the speaker’s own opinion without support.
A dream sequence treated as literal real-world intent.
A documentary explanation treated as promotion.
Praise or normalization treated as neutral description.
Indirect speech treated as a direct statement without support.
common_false_positives: Indirect encouragement or indirect threat flattened into neutral speech.

glossary_relationships.note: Intent is the central meaning question.
Motivation can support approval or promotion.
Quoted speech may not represent endorsement.
Documentation and documentary framing reduce the force of apparent endorsement.
Mockery often behaves like satire, sarcasm, or irony.
Praise can strengthen approval or glorification.
Normalization can strengthen promotion when harmful conduct is presented as ordinary.
A threat may be recoverable only through context.
Encouragement may be recoverable only through context.
Condemnation can neutralize apparent harmful content.

article_mapping.note: Approval, praise, promotion, glorification, threat, coercion, and similar stances.
Direct, indirect, and normalized promotion in content standards.
Promotion of banned groups and their normalization.
Dreams, acting, role play, humor, and story framing.

reporting_guidance: Explain the scene-level intent before the legal outcome.
Mention any quotation, fiction, educational, documentary, or condemnation exception explicitly.
Distinguish documentary explanation from endorsement, and mockery from direct hostility.
If encouragement or threat is indirect, say how the scene recovers that reading.
Call out praise, glorification, or normalization when the wording presents harmful conduct as admirable or ordinary.
Use confidence to reflect how strongly the scene supports the final reading.
